nodes.name: Weight decay (Hanson-Pratt)
nodes.section: 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-based Update
nodes.statement_latex: Weight decay updates the weights as $\bm{\theta}_{t+1} = (1 - \lambda) \bm{\theta}_t - \alpha \nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_t)$, where $\lambda$ is the per-step decay rate and $\alpha$ the learning rate.
nodes.statement_clean: Weights decay multiplicatively by $(1-\lambda)$ at each step before the gradient update.

nodes.name: $L_2$ regularization
nodes.section: 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-based Update
nodes.statement_latex: Augment the batch loss with a quadratic penalty: $f_{t}^{\text{reg}}(\bm{\theta}) = f_t(\bm{\theta}) + \frac{\lambda'}{2} \norm{\bm{\theta}}_2^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Add a quadratic penalty on the weights to the loss.

nodes.name: Schedule multiplier $\eta_t$
nodes.section: 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-based Update
nodes.statement_latex: $\eta_t = \text{SetScheduleMultiplier}(t)$ is a user-defined multiplier scaling both $\alpha$ and $\lambda$, allowing fixed, decay, or warm-restart schedules.
nodes.statement_clean: A scalar that rescales the learning rate and weight-decay factor over iterations.

nodes.name: Adaptive gradient algorithm with preconditioner $\mathbf{M}_t$
nodes.section: 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-based Update
nodes.statement_latex: An optimizer $O$ with iterates $\bm{\theta}_{t+1} \leftarrow \bm{\theta}_t - \alpha \mathbf{M}_t \nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_t)$, where $\mathbf{M}_t$ is a (typically time-varying) preconditioner matrix.
nodes.statement_clean: An SGD variant that scales gradients by a preconditioner $\mathbf{M}_t$.

nodes.name: Normalized weight decay $\lambda_{norm}$
nodes.section: Appendix B.1 Normalized Weight Decay
nodes.statement_latex: Reparameterize $\lambda = \lambda_{norm} \sqrt{ b / (B T) }$, where $b$ is batch size, $B$ the number of training points, and $T$ the total number of epochs. Then $\lambda_{norm}$ is the weight decay used if only one batch pass is allowed.
nodes.statement_clean: A budget-invariant rescaling of the weight-decay factor.

nodes.name: Cosine annealing schedule
nodes.section: Appendix B.2 Adam with Cosine Annealing and Warm Restarts
nodes.statement_latex: $\eta_t = \eta^{(i)}_{min} + 0.5 (\eta^{(i)}_{max} - \eta^{(i)}_{min}) (1 + \cos(\pi T_{cur} / T_i))$, simplifying to $\eta_t = 0.5 + 0.5\cos(\pi T_{cur} / T_i)$ when $\eta^{(i)}_{min}=0,\eta^{(i)}_{max}=1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Schedule that anneals the multiplier from $\eta_{max}$ to $\eta_{min}$ along a half-cosine.

nodes.name: Warm restart (SGDR)
nodes.section: Appendix B.2 Adam with Cosine Annealing and Warm Restarts
nodes.statement_latex: After $T_i$ epochs, reset $T_{cur} = 0$ so the multiplier $\eta_t$ jumps back toward $\eta^{(i)}_{max}$, while keeping the current $\bm{\theta}_t$ as initialization; the next budget is $T_{i+1} = T_i \cdot T_{mult}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Periodically reset the schedule to its peak while keeping the current weights.

nodes.name: Decoupled weight-decay update
nodes.section: 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-based Update
nodes.statement_latex: $\bm{\theta}_{t+1} = (1 - \lambda) \bm{\theta}_t - \alpha \nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_t)$ (Eq. \ref{eq:wdecay}).

nodes.name: Aitchison Bayesian filtering update
nodes.section: 3 Justification via Bayesian Filtering
nodes.statement_latex: $\bm{\mu}_{post} = \bm{\mu}_{prior} + \bm{\Sigma}_{post} \bm{g}$, with state transition $P(\bm{\theta}_{t+1} \mid \bm{\theta}_t) = \mathcal{N}((\bm{I}-\bm{A}) \bm{\theta}_t, \bm{Q})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Posterior mean update for filtering, with $(\bm{I}-\bm{A})$ playing the role of decoupled weight decay when $\bm{A}=\lambda\bm{I}$.

nodes.name: SGDW (SGD with momentum and decoupled weight decay)
nodes.section: 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-based Update (Algorithm 1)
nodes.statement_latex: Stochastic gradient descent with momentum where the weight-decay step $-\eta_t \lambda \bm{\theta}_{t-1}$ is decoupled from (and not folded into) the gradient $\vc{g}_t$.

nodes.name: AdamW (Adam with decoupled weight decay)
nodes.section: 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-based Update (Algorithm 2)
nodes.statement_latex: Adam in which the weight-decay term $-\eta_t \lambda \bm{\theta}_{t-1}$ is added directly to the parameter update (line 12), separately from the adaptive Adam step $\alpha \hat{\vc{m}}_t / (\sqrt{\hat{\vc{v}}_t} + \epsilon)$.

nodes.name: AdamWR (AdamW with warm restarts and normalized weight decay)
nodes.section: Appendix B.2 Adam with Cosine Annealing and Warm Restarts
nodes.statement_latex: AdamW (Algorithm 2) with $\eta_t$ following the cosine schedule of Eq.\ \ref{eq:t2} and $\lambda$ recomputed each iteration via the normalized weight decay $\lambda = \lambda_{norm} \sqrt{b / (B T)}$.
output: Optimized parameters $\bm{\theta}_t$, with snapshots taken before each restart

nodes.name: Adam (with $L_2$ regularization)
nodes.section: 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-based Update (Algorithm 2, baseline)
nodes.statement_latex: Standard Adam in which the regularization is implemented by adding $\lambda \bm{\theta}_{t-1}$ to the gradient $\vc{g}_t$ before the moment estimates are formed.

nodes.name: Weight decay = $L_2$ reg for standard SGD
nodes.section: 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-based Update (Proposition 1)
nodes.statement_latex: Standard SGD with base learning rate $\alpha$ on $f_t(\bm{\theta})$ with weight decay $\lambda$ executes the same steps as SGD without weight decay on $f_{t}^{\text{reg}}(\bm{\theta}) = f_t(\bm{\theta}) + \frac{\lambda'}{2} \norm{\bm{\theta}}_2^2$, with $\lambda' = \lambda/\alpha$.
assumptions: Optimizer is standard SGD (no preconditioner) with base learning rate $\alpha$
Weight decay $\lambda$ defined as in Eq.\ \ref{eq:wdecay}

nodes.name: Weight decay $\neq$ $L_2$ reg for adaptive gradients
nodes.section: 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-based Update (Proposition 2)
nodes.statement_latex:
Let $O$ be an optimizer with iterates $ m{	heta}_{t+1} \leftarrow  m{	heta}_t - \alpha \mathbf{M}_t 
abla f_t( m{	heta}_t)$ (no decay) and $ m{	heta}_{t+1} \leftarrow (1 - \lambda)  m{	heta}_t - \alpha \mathbf{M}_t 
abla f_t( m{	heta}_t)$ (with decay), with $\mathbf{M}_t 
eq k \mathbf{I}$. Then no $L_2$ coefficient $\lambda'$ makes running $O$ on $f_t +  rac{\lambda'}{2}
orm{ m{	heta}}_2^2$ equivalent to running $O$ on $f_t$ with weight decay $\lambda \in \R^+$.
conclusions: No $\lambda'$ exists making $L_2$ regularization equivalent to weight decay for $O$

nodes.name: Weight decay = scale-adjusted $L_2$ reg for fixed preconditioner
nodes.section: 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-based Update (Proposition 3)
nodes.statement_latex: If $O$ has the iterates of Proposition 2 with fixed preconditioner $\mathbf{M}_t = \text{diag}(\vc{s})^{-1}$, $s_i > 0$, then $O$ on $f_t$ with weight decay $\lambda$ executes the same steps as $O$ without decay on $f_{t}^{\text{sreg}}(\bm{\theta}) = f_t(\bm{\theta}) + \frac{\lambda'}{2\alpha} \norm{\bm{\theta} \odot \sqrt{\vc{s}}}_2^2$, with $\lambda' = \lambda/\alpha$.
conclusions: Weight decay $\lambda$ is equivalent to a scale-adjusted $L_2$ regularizer with $\lambda' = \lambda/\alpha$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1
nodes.section: Appendix A Formal Analysis (Proof of Prop 1)
nodes.statement_latex:
Direct expansion: SGD on $f_t +  rac{\lambda'}{2}
orm{ m{	heta}}_2^2$ yields $ m{	heta}_{t+1} =  m{	heta}_t - \alpha 
abla f_t - \alpha \lambda'  m{	heta}_t$, while SGD with weight decay yields $(1-\lambda) m{	heta}_t - \alpha 
abla f_t$. The two coincide iff $\lambda' = \lambda/\alpha$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2
nodes.section: Appendix A Formal Analysis (Proof of Prop 2)
nodes.statement_latex: Compare iterates with and without decay; equality for all $\bm{\theta}_t$ would require $\lambda \bm{\theta}_t = \alpha \lambda' \mathbf{M}_t \bm{\theta}_t$, which can hold for arbitrary $\bm{\theta}_t$ only if $\mathbf{M}_t = k \mathbf{I}$, contradicting the hypothesis.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3
nodes.section: Appendix A Formal Analysis (Proof of Prop 3)
nodes.statement_latex: Compute the iterates of $O$ on $f_{t}^{\text{sreg}}$ without decay and on $f_t$ with decay; both reduce to $\bm{\theta}_t - \alpha \nabla f_t / \vc{s} - \lambda \bm{\theta}_t$ once $\lambda' = \lambda/\alpha$ is substituted.

nodes.name: Expand SGD step on $L_2$-regularized loss
nodes.statement_latex: $\bm{\theta}_{t+1} \leftarrow \bm{\theta}_t - \alpha \nabla f_{t}^{\text{reg}}(\bm{\theta}_t) = \bm{\theta}_t - \alpha \nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_t) - \alpha \lambda' \bm{\theta}_t$.

nodes.name: Write SGD step with weight decay
nodes.statement_latex: $\bm{\theta}_{t+1} \leftarrow (1 - \lambda) \bm{\theta}_t - \alpha \nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_t) = \bm{\theta}_t - \lambda \bm{\theta}_t - \alpha \nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_t)$.

nodes.name: Match coefficients
nodes.statement_latex: Identifying $\alpha \lambda' \bm{\theta}_t$ with $\lambda \bm{\theta}_t$ gives $\lambda' = \lambda/\alpha$, so the two iterations coincide.

nodes.name: Write iterate of $O$ on $L_2$-regularized $f_t$
nodes.statement_latex: $\bm{\theta}_{t+1} \leftarrow \bm{\theta}_t - \alpha \lambda' \mathbf{M}_t \bm{\theta}_t - \alpha \mathbf{M}_t \nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_t)$.

nodes.name: Write iterate of $O$ with decoupled weight decay
nodes.statement_latex: $\bm{\theta}_{t+1} \leftarrow (1 - \lambda) \bm{\theta}_t - \alpha \mathbf{M}_t \nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_t)$.

nodes.name: Equate the two and derive contradiction
nodes.statement_latex: Equality for all $\bm{\theta}_t$ requires $\lambda \bm{\theta}_t = \alpha \lambda' \mathbf{M}_t \bm{\theta}_t$, which holds for arbitrary $\bm{\theta}_t$ only if $\mathbf{M}_t = k\mathbf{I}$ for some $k \in \R$ \textemdash{} contradiction. Hence no such $\lambda'$ exists.

nodes.name: Expand iterate of $O$ on $f_{t}^{\text{sreg}}$
nodes.statement_latex: Without decay, $\bm{\theta}_{t+1} \leftarrow \bm{\theta}_t - \alpha \nabla f_{t}^{\text{sreg}}(\bm{\theta}_t)/\vc{s} = \bm{\theta}_t - \alpha \nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_t)/\vc{s} - \alpha \lambda' \bm{\theta}_t$.

nodes.name: Expand iterate of $O$ with weight decay
nodes.statement_latex: With weight decay on $f_t$, $\bm{\theta}_{t+1} \leftarrow (1 - \lambda) \bm{\theta}_t - \alpha \nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_t)/\vc{s} = \bm{\theta}_t - \lambda \bm{\theta}_t - \alpha \nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_t)/\vc{s}$.

nodes.name: Match coefficients
nodes.statement_latex: Setting $\alpha \lambda' = \lambda$, i.e.\ $\lambda' = \lambda/\alpha$, makes the two iterates identical.

nodes.name: Initialize
nodes.statement_latex: Set $t \leftarrow 0$, $\bm{\theta}_{t=0} \in \R^n$, $\vc{m}_{t=0} \leftarrow \vc{0}$, $\eta_{t=0} \in \R$.

nodes.name: Main loop
nodes.statement_latex: Repeat until stopping: $t \leftarrow t+1$; sample batch and gradient $\nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_{t-1})$; set $\vc{g}_t \leftarrow \nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_{t-1})$ (the $L_2$ variant adds $+\lambda \bm{\theta}_{t-1}$ here); set $\eta_t \leftarrow \text{SetScheduleMultiplier}(t)$.

nodes.name: Momentum and decoupled-decay update
nodes.statement_latex: $\vc{m}_t \leftarrow \beta_1 \vc{m}_{t-1} + \eta_t \alpha \vc{g}_t$;  $\bm{\theta}_t \leftarrow \bm{\theta}_{t-1} - \vc{m}_t - \eta_t \lambda \bm{\theta}_{t-1}$ (the decoupled weight-decay term).

nodes.name: Return
nodes.statement_latex: Return optimized parameters $\bm{\theta}_t$.

nodes.name: Initialize
nodes.statement_latex: Set $t \leftarrow 0$, $\bm{\theta}_{t=0} \in \R^n$, $\vc{m}_{t=0} \leftarrow \vc{0}$, $\vc{v}_{t=0} \leftarrow \vc{0}$, $\eta_{t=0} \in \R$.

nodes.name: Main loop: gradient and moment estimates
nodes.statement_latex: Repeat: $t \leftarrow t+1$; $\vc{g}_t \leftarrow \nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_{t-1})$ (Adam-$L_2$ adds $+\lambda \bm{\theta}_{t-1}$); $\vc{m}_t \leftarrow \beta_1 \vc{m}_{t-1} + (1-\beta_1) \vc{g}_t$; $\vc{v}_t \leftarrow \beta_2 \vc{v}_{t-1} + (1-\beta_2) \vc{g}_t^2$.

nodes.name: Bias correction
nodes.statement_latex: $\hat{\vc{m}}_t \leftarrow \vc{m}_t / (1 - \beta_1^t)$, $\hat{\vc{v}}_t \leftarrow \vc{v}_t / (1 - \beta_2^t)$.

nodes.name: Schedule multiplier and decoupled-decay parameter update
nodes.statement_latex: $\eta_t \leftarrow \text{SetScheduleMultiplier}(t)$; $\bm{\theta}_t \leftarrow \bm{\theta}_{t-1} - \eta_t \big( \alpha \hat{\vc{m}}_t / (\sqrt{\hat{\vc{v}}_t} + \epsilon) + \lambda \bm{\theta}_{t-1} \big)$, decoupling the weight-decay term from the adaptive Adam step.

nodes.name: Return
nodes.statement_latex: Return optimized parameters $\bm{\theta}_t$.

nodes.name: Compute weight decay from normalized $\lambda_{norm}$
nodes.statement_latex: At each iteration set $\lambda \leftarrow \lambda_{norm} \sqrt{ b / (B T_i) }$, where $T_i$ is the length of the current restart.

nodes.name: Cosine-annealed schedule multiplier
nodes.statement_latex: Set $\eta_t = 0.5 + 0.5 \cos(\pi T_{cur}/T_i)$ (Eq.\ \ref{eq:t2}) and use it inside the AdamW update.

nodes.name: Run AdamW iteration
nodes.statement_latex: Execute one step of AdamW (Algorithm 2) with the current $\eta_t$ and $\lambda$.

nodes.name: Restart trigger
nodes.statement_latex: When $T_{cur} = T_i$, snapshot $\bm{\theta}_t$, set $T_{cur} \leftarrow 0$ and $T_{i+1} \leftarrow T_i \cdot T_{mult}$, then continue with the new restart.

nodes.name: Train deep networks with adaptive gradient methods that generalize as well as SGD with momentum
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_latex: Find a regularization scheme for adaptive gradient optimizers (Adam, etc.) that closes the generalization gap to SGD with momentum on image classification benchmarks while keeping hyperparameter tuning tractable.

nodes.name: AdamW vs Adam on CIFAR-10 (26 2x64d ResNet, 100 epochs)
nodes.section: 5.1 Evaluating Decoupled Weight Decay With Different Learning Rate Schedules (Figure 1)
nodes.statement_latex: Training a 26 2x64d ResNet on CIFAR-10 for 100 epochs under fixed, drop-step, and cosine-annealing schedules; AdamW yields lower test error than Adam-$L_2$ across all three, and the gap widens with better schedules.

nodes.name: Hyperparameter landscape on CIFAR-10 (Figure 2)
nodes.section: 5.2 Decoupling the Weight Decay and Initial Learning Rate Parameters
nodes.statement_latex: On CIFAR-10 with a 26 2x64d ResNet for 100 epochs, the basin of best $(\alpha,\lambda)$ settings lies on the diagonal for SGD/Adam with $L_2$ but is axis-aligned for SGDW/AdamW, demonstrating decoupling of $\lambda$ from $\alpha$.

nodes.name: Long-run generalization on CIFAR-10 (1800 epochs, Figure 3)
nodes.section: 5.3 Better Generalization of AdamW
nodes.statement_latex: A 26 2x96d ResNet trained for 1800 epochs with $\alpha=0.001$ and 12 (Adam) / 7 (AdamW) settings of weight decay; AdamW yields lower training loss \emph{and} better test error at matched training loss, an absolute 15\% relative test-error improvement.

nodes.name: AdamWR warm restarts on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet32x32 (Figure 4)
nodes.section: 5.4 AdamWR with Warm Restarts for Better Anytime Performance
nodes.statement_latex: AdamWR matches AdamW's final accuracy while reaching it up to $10\times$ faster on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet32x32; closes most of the gap to SGDWR on CIFAR-10.

nodes.name: Normalized weight decay across budgets and datasets (SuppFigure 4)
nodes.section: Appendix C Additional Results
nodes.statement_latex: Optimal raw $\lambda$ shifts strongly with the number of epochs and across CIFAR-10/ImageNet32x32, but optimal $\lambda_{norm}$ is nearly invariant ($\lambda_{norm}\in\{0.025, 0.05\}$ across SGDW and AdamW).

nodes.name: Intuition: $L_2$ under-regularizes weights with large historical gradients in Adam
nodes.section: 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-based Update
nodes.statement_latex: When Adam runs on $f + \frac{\lambda'}{2}\norm{\bm{\theta}}_2^2$, the regularizer's gradient is normalized by the same $\sqrt{\hat{\vc{v}}_t}$ as the loss gradient, so weights with large typical gradient amplitudes are effectively regularized less than they would be under decoupled weight decay.

nodes.name: Aitchison Bayesian-filtering justification of decoupled weight decay
nodes.section: 3 Justification via Bayesian Filtering
nodes.statement_latex: In Aitchison's Bayesian-filtering view of adaptive gradients, instantiating the state-transition regularizer as $\bm{A} = \lambda \bm{I}$ in $P(\bm{\theta}_{t+1}\mid\bm{\theta}_t)=\mathcal{N}((\bm{I}-\bm{A})\bm{\theta}_t,\bm{Q})$ produces decoupled weight decay; this regularizer applies to the prior independently of the per-parameter posterior uncertainty, whereas $L_2$ regularization would entangle them.

nodes.name: Proposition 3 is suggestive, not directly applicable
nodes.section: 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-based Update
nodes.statement_latex: Proposition 3 fixes the preconditioner, while practical adaptive methods change $\mathbf{M}_t$ each step. The proposition still gives intuition: parameters with large $s_i$ (historically large gradients) are regularized in proportion to $\sqrt{s_i}$, more strongly than under standard $L_2$.

nodes.name: Cited downstream uses of AdamW
nodes.section: 5.5 Use of AdamW on other datasets and architectures
nodes.statement_latex: AdamW has been adopted by external groups: face detection on WIDER FACE \citep{2018arXiv180406559W}, intracranial-EEG classification \citep{volker2018intracranial} (e.g. 73.68\% vs 71.37\% on Deep4Net), Transformer pretraining \citep{radford2018improving}, and the K-FAC comparison of \citet{zhang2018three}.
